Maria (CS): FYI customer BrightBank reporting dramatically increased latency and auth failures — says requests are hitting us-east even though they configured eu-west.
Oliver (SRE): Can you paste a request id and sample timestamps? Also any proxy headers they set (X-Region / X-Client-Region)?
Maria (CS): Here are two recent request IDs: req_01GZ9A4Y8D4X1, req_01GZ9B2K5H7M3. Customer provided curl they use:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_..." \
  -H "X-Target-Region: eu-west-1" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-open-7b","input":"hello"}'
```
They say response headers show Location: us-east-1 and latency ~1200ms.
Nina (Support): Adding raw log from their session (sanitized):
```
2026-03-10T15:21:43Z req_01GZ9A4Y8D4X1 route_decision=us-east-1 fallback_reason=quota_exhausted cached_route=us-east-1
```
Liam (Runtime Eng): That fallback_reason value is interesting — should only trigger when eu pool is fully saturated. Can we check eu-west capacity and the routing cache entries around that time?
Oliver (SRE): Checking autoscaler + routing cache now. Quick snapshot: eu-west pool at 68% GPU utilization at 15:21Z, no recent scale events. But routing cache has a sticky entry for BrightBank with TTL=7d created 2025-11-02T... looks wrong.
Diego (Infra): I suspect sticky routing cache bug — when a customer pins a region via header we create a sticky mapping, but an earlier migration changed TTL calculation to persist across region changes. That could cause old us-east sticky mappings to survive and override header-based routing.
Maria (CS): Customer insists they never used us-east. They started a monthly Dedicated reservation last week — could that have triggered a migration event?
Liam (Runtime Eng): Yes — Dedicated onboarding triggers a quick rebind that should clear stickies. There's a race where rebind + sticky write can create an inconsistent mapping. Repro attempt:
1) Create sticky mapping for account A -> us-east
2) Perform rebind to eu-west
3) If a sticky write races after rebind, the mapping reverts to us-east
Repro curl snippet:
```bash
# simulate rebind then concurrent sticky write
http POST https://internal-routing.redwood/v1/sticky account=acct_brightbank region=us-east-1 &
# then rebind
http POST https://internal-routing.redwood/v1/rebind account=acct_brightbank region=eu-west-1
```
Oliver (SRE): Confirmed repro in staging. The routing worker writes stickies without verifying the rebind generation id. When rebind increments generation, sticky write should be conditional on matching generation.
Nina (Support): For BrightBank right now — any quick mitigation we can advise them to do so they get eu-west routing immediately?
Diego (Infra): Temporary workaround: instruct them to include header "X-Force-Region: eu-west-1" which our gateway honors before sticky mapping for 2 minutes and will bypass the stale sticky. Also we can expire their sticky manually from routing admin UI.
Maria (CS): I told BrightBank the workaround and will expire their sticky now.
Maria (CS): Done — confirmed with customer they now see Location: eu-west-1 and latency ~80ms. Customer appreciates the quick fix.
Liam (Runtime Eng): Permanent fix: make sticky write conditional on rebind generation id + add an e2e test that rebind + concurrent sticky writes do not revert mapping. I'll open PR to runtime this afternoon.
Diego (Infra): I'll add a small migration script to expire any stickies older than 30d and add an alert if sticky writes spike post-rebind.
Oliver (SRE): Filing incident ticket and postmortem. Action items:
- runtime: conditional sticky write + unit/e2e (owner: Liam) — ETA 48h
- infra: migration to expire old stickies + alert (owner: Diego) — ETA 72h
- support: follow-up with BrightBank + confirm SLA impact (owner: Maria) — ETA 24h
- ops: add temporary dashboard for sticky mapping counts (owner: Oliver) — ETA 24h
Maria (CS): I'll draft the customer follow-up and include root cause + workaround + timeline.
